mercy_translation.text:
Let these things, then, be set before you from us in a few words, as far as an elementary outline and pattern of the faith according to Christ and of his divine manifestation toward us, O lover of Christ.

Taking your starting point from these things, if you read the writings of the Scriptures and sincerely fix your mind upon them, you will learn from them more perfectly and clearly the exact truth of what has been said.

For those Scriptures were spoken and written from God through men who spoke of divine things. And we, having learned from inspired teachers who read them—teachers who also became witnesses to the divinity of Christ—share what we have received with your love of learning.

You will also come to know his second manifestation toward us, glorious and truly divine, when he will come no longer in humility but in his own glory; no longer in lowliness but in his own majesty; no longer to suffer, but now to give to all the fruit of his own cross—I mean resurrection and incorruption. He will no longer be judged, but will judge all according to what each has done through the body, whether good or evil. There the kingdom of heaven is laid up for those who have done good, while for those who have done evil there are eternal fire and outer darkness.

For the Lord himself says: “I tell you, from now on you shall see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming upon the clouds of heaven in the glory of the Father.”

Therefore there is also a saving word that prepares us for that day and says: “Be ready and watch, for at an hour you do not know he comes.” For according to the blessed Paul, “we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each may receive according to what he has done through the body, whether good or evil.”

translator_notes: Translated directly from the Greek source.
The final chapter directs the reader back to Scripture and frames Athanasius' treatise as an introductory outline rather than an exhaustive account.
The chapter closes with the second coming, resurrection, incorruption, judgment, and moral readiness.
